chapter: Leaving Hampton: Europe and Los Angeles
title: Leaving Indianapolis to escape segregation
summary: Monk could not readjust to Indianapolis, where black patrons were barred from clubs, and was resolved to be a professional musician elsewhere.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: There was less prejudice. You know, in Indianapolis at that time we had...The blacks couldn't go into certain clubs. It was still that dark shadow over that whole scene. We couldn't go out to this club, or somebody couldn't go in that club because...But the whites could come into any of the clubs. And they come down to the Avenue and catch all the jazz scenes. And they had to come and hang with us but we couldn't ever go back out to where they was at. So I couldn't go. I just couldn't bring myself to go back with that kind of...readjust back to that kind of attitude.

And I wanted to...it was no question in my mind that my future was going to be involved with music. I was going to be a professional musician. There's no question about, 'Well, I've tried it and now I'm going back to the foundry.' There was no such thing. From that point on, I was going to be a musician. So I needed to get in an environment that's going to be better for what I was going to do, for my head and everything else. So...
